item.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption surveyed 502 randomly selected NSW adults in November 1993 about corruption and understanding and support of its work.
item.support:
in November 1993 a survey was
conducted of a random sample of the NSW adult population.

item.text: The survey examined perceived corruption, its effects, reporting attitudes and awareness and opinions of ICAC.
item.support: In order to obtain information about the public's perceptions of corruption

item.text: ICAC reported that 55% considered public sector corruption a serious problem and 37% considered it a minor problem.
item.support: 55% considered corruption in the NSW public sector to be a serious problem

item.text: ICAC reported that 92% supported its existence, while 80% considered it successful at exposing corruption and 53% at reducing it.
item.support:
53% considered that the Commission had been successful or very successful in reducing
some of the corruption

item.quote:
68% disagreed or strongly disagreed that There is no point in reporting corruption in the
NSW public sector because nothing useful will be done about it.
